heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P can print Polymaker PolyLite ASA at up to 202 mm/s based on a 17 mm³/s volumetric flow limit, but its open-frame design makes parts prone to severe warping and layer separation. Adding an enclosure or printing strictly small parts with a draft shield is essential to combat temperature-induced shrinkage.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Liquid Glue or PVP Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Bed Temperature to 98°C for all layers and increase First Layer Height to 0.24mm to maximize mechanical bed adhesion.
Cap Part Cooling Fan to 0% base and 15-20% maximum for overhangs, ensuring the aux fan is set to 0% to avoid premature layer delamination.
Enable a Draft Shield (Auto or Tall) in the Others tab with 2 loops to insulate open-frame ambient airflow from the part.
Clamp Max Volumetric Speed to 17 mm³/s in the filament settings and calibrate Pressure Advance to approximately 0.038.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and print warping off the bed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High thermal shrinkage coefficient of ASA interacting with ambient room drafts on the open-frame P1P chassis.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply PVP glue stick to a cleaned textured PEI plate, raise bed temperature to 98°C, add a 5mm outer brim, and activate a draft shield.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer splitting and delamination along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Overcooling from chamber draft or excessive cooling fan speed causing incomplete polymer cross-fusion between layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Disable the auxiliary part cooling fan completely, limit main part cooling fan to a 0-15% threshold, and increase nozzle temperature to 255°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Surface popping, roughness, and stringing across travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the hygroscopic ASA polymer during storage or extended printing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated blast or desiccant dryer at 70°C for at least 6 hours prior to printing and lower nozzle temp to 250°C.

faq.question: Can I print large ASA parts on an unmodified P1P?
faq.answer: No, printing large footprint or tall ASA parts on a stock P1P usually fails due to rapid thermal contraction and splitting without an enclosure.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for PolyLite ASA?
faq.answer: No, unmodified PolyLite ASA is non-abrasive, so the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears are fully adequate.

faq.question: Are the fumes from printing ASA dangerous without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, ASA releases styrene gas and ultra-fine particles; print only in a well-ventilated room, next to a window exhaust, or inside an enclosed, filtered printer.

faq.question: Why does OrcaSlicer cap my print speeds below the P1P maximum limits?
faq.answer: The filament profile restricts volumetric flow to 17 mm³/s, which caps actual linear speeds at 202 mm/s for a 0.4mm nozzle at 0.2mm layer height to ensure consistent extrusion.
